summary: The District continues grappling with the aftermath of a year-long National Guard deployment, with advocacy groups citing the federal military presence as evidence for statehood, while the Department of Justice has opposed the D.C. Council's efforts to demand withdrawal. Separately, D.C. Vote is pushing back against what it characterizes as a congressional threat to the District's fiscal independence. Without statehood, D.C. does not control its own National Guard and cannot refuse the deployment of other states' troops within its borders.
